commit.message:
input: fall back to last caret for IME candidate bounds before repaint (#3286) (#3297)

Closes #3286

### Problem
When composing text with an IME in `InputBaseState` (e.g., `Textarea` or
`Input`), newly inserted or marked text offsets may not yet be shaped in
`last_layout` prior to the subsequent repaint. In `bounds_for_range`,
querying `line.position_for_index` for offsets outside `last_layout`
returns `None`.

Previously, `start_origin` and `end_origin` both fell back via
`unwrap_or_default()`, resetting their origins to `(0, 0)`. This caused:
1. Candidate windows to jump horizontally back to the input origin
before repainting.
2. If `start_origin` was resolved within `last_layout` but `end_origin`
fell past the layout, `end_origin` defaulted to `(0, 0)`, producing
inverted or full-width bounds.

### Solution
1. In `bounds_for_range`, when `start_origin` cannot be resolved within
`last_layout`, fall back to the position of `self.last_cursor` (or
`self.cursor()`) from the previous layout.
2. Default `end_origin` to `start_origin` rather than `(0, 0)` so that
unresolved end offsets remain anchored at the caret rather than jumping
to the left margin.
3. Added a regression unit test
`test_ime_candidate_bounds_fallback_before_repaint` validating that
candidate bounds stay within proximity of the caret before repaint.

commit.message:
website: Fail a docs test on a hand-written GPUI Kit version (#3353)

## Summary

Adds the missing half of the documentation-version guard.
`website/tests/doc-sources.test.ts` already fails a pull request that
writes out the GPUI snapshot version by hand (`{{gpui_pre_version}}`),
and `doc-variables.js` provides `{{gpui_kit_version}}` for the same
reason — but nothing checked that pages actually *use* it. So `v0.7.0`
shipped with a hand-written `gpui-kit = "0.6"` in 20 places across 14
pages in both locales, and `/docs/installation/` still serves it today.

Refs #3340. **This does not fix the live page** — see below.

## What #3340 actually is

The report asks for the docs to show `gpui-kit = "0.7"`, and suggests
the published site is "a stale build (or an incorrect `GPUI_KIT_VERSION`
/ snapshot)". I don't think that diagnosis holds:

- The version resolver is correct. `readGpuiKitVersion()` prefers
`GPUI_KIT_VERSION`, which `script/build-website-versions` sets from the
tag, and `/` is built with `GPUI_KIT_VERSION="$(gpui_kit_version
"$latest_release")"` where `latest_release` is `v0.7.0`. That resolves
to `0.7.0`.
- But `/` is built from **`snapshot_website "$latest_release"`** — the
Markdown *at the tag*, not from `main`. At `v0.7.0`,
`website/docs/installation.md:54` reads `gpui-kit = "0.6"` and contains
no `{{gpui_kit_version}}` at all (0 occurrences). The placeholder landed
on `main` after the tag.
- So the literal in the live page is the literal in the `v0.7.0` tag,
and it will keep being served until the next release. Editing `main`
cannot change it, and re-tagging a published release is not something a
contributor PR should do.

What I can do without touching the release process is stop it from
recurring.

## The guard

One test, in the idiom of the `gpui_pre_version` one beside it. It
matches only the forms that actually encode the dependency:

- a Cargo declaration, bare (`gpui-kit = "0.7"`) or table (`gpui-kit = {
version = "0.7", features = [...] }`)
- a `docs.rs` link pinned to a version

and reports `use {{gpui_kit_version}}`.

Deliberately **not** matched, because matching them produces noise
rather than signal: `gpui-kit-assets` (the `(?!-)` after the crate
name), `docs.rs/gpui-kit/latest`, and prose that mentions the crate next
to an unrelated version. I first tried the looser shape the
`gpui_pre_version` test uses — flag any `\d+\.\d+` on a line containing
`gpui-pre` — and it produced six false positives on `main`
(`comparison.md` citing Zed `0.14.0`, `webassembly.md` citing
wasm-bindgen `0.2.121`, `fonts.md` citing a Rust edition). Those would
have needed `INTENTIONAL_GPUI_PINS`-style allowlist entries for crates
that have nothing to do with Kit.

## Verification

The guard passes on `main` (0 hits) and fails against the real `v0.7.0`
documentation, checked out as a worktree and run with the same `bun
test`:

```
main        0 hits
v0.7.0      20 hits, e.g.
            docs/installation.md:54 writes a GPUI Kit version — use {{gpui_kit_version}}
            docs/getting-started.md:22 writes a GPUI Kit version — use {{gpui_kit_version}}
            zh-CN/docs/installation.md:54 writes a GPUI Kit version — use {{gpui_kit_version}}
            … (9 per locale)
```

`bun run test:docs`: the two `markdownLinks` tests time out at bun's 5s
default on this machine, and fail identically on the unmodified tree —
pre-existing, and CI does not hit it. Everything else in that script
passes with this change (7 pass vs 2 pass before, same 2 pre-existing
failures).

`bunx tsc --noEmit` reports only pre-existing errors under `src/`;
nothing in `website/tests/`.

## Not done, and why

- **The live `/` page still says `0.6`.** Only a new release fixes that.
If you want it fixed sooner, the options are to backport the placeholder
onto a `v0.6.6`-style maintenance branch and cut a new patch tag, or to
build `/` from `main` — the latter changes what "the docs at `/`" mean,
so I did not go near it. Happy to do either if you want it.
- No release pipeline, `script/build-website-versions`, or docs content
is changed. The only file touched is the test.

## Public API

None. Test-only change; no crate, TypeScript declaration, or exported
symbol is added or altered.

## Notes

Written with `opencode/space-bunny-free`.

commit.message:
clipboard: Add accessibility_label to name the icon button (#3354)

## Description

`Clipboard` renders an icon-only `Button`. Without an accessible name,
screen readers announced it as just "button", and accessibility-driven
UI tests could not find it by name. The accessibility guide requires a
name on icon-only buttons.

`Clipboard` now gives its button the existing localized "Copy" name by
default. Applications can use `Clipboard::accessibility_label` for a
more specific name, such as "Copy API key". The tooltip remains a
separate hint and is not used as the name. The English and Chinese
Clipboard docs show the default and contextual override.

## Screenshot

No visual change. This only adds an accessible name.

## Public API

### gpui-component

- `gpui_component::clipboard::Clipboard::accessibility_label(self,
label: impl Into<SharedString>) -> Self`: overrides the default
localized "Copy" name with a context-specific name for the clipboard
button.

## How to Test

- `cargo test -p gpui-kit --features gpui-kit/test-support --locked
--test components` — 4 passed locally, including
`clipboard_reports_default_and_explicit_accessibility_names`. It checks
that an unnamed `Clipboard` announces "Copy" and an explicit name
overrides it. The default-name assertion failed before the follow-up
fix.
- `cargo clippy -p gpui-component -p gpui-kit --all-targets --features
gpui-kit/test-support --locked -- --deny warnings` — passed locally.
- `cargo check -p gpui-component --no-default-features --locked` —
passed locally.
- `rustfmt --check crates/component/src/clipboard.rs
crates/kit/tests/components.rs` and `git diff --check` — passed locally.
- `cargo run -- clipboard`: the Clipboard story renders and works as
before (author's original manual check).

## Checklist

- [x] I have read the [CONTRIBUTING](../CONTRIBUTING.md) document and
followed the guidelines.
- [x] Reviewed the changes in this PR and confirmed AI generated code
(If any) is accurate.
- [x] Passed `cargo run` for story tests related to the changes.

commit.message:
input: report inline token hover for tooltips and previews (#3346)

Closes #3335

## Description

Adds `on_token_hover` for the atomic inline tokens rendered in `Input`
and `Textarea`, so hovering over a token can render a tooltip, preview,
or run custom logic.

The change follows the existing `on_token_click` seam: `gpui-base` owns
hover hit-testing, token geometry, and the hover snapshot event, while
`gpui-component` only forwards the builder and the application owns the
tooltip itself. Hover never selects or edits the document. Disabled
tokens never report hover entry, matching click; readonly tokens do.
Works for both `Input`/`InputState` and `Textarea`/`TextareaState`, plus
the JavaScript bindings.

Hover exit is delivered even when the hovered token is removed or
replaced programmatically (even at the same offset), scrolled out of the
laid-out rows, masked, or disabled: the state retains the last hovered
token snapshot and reconciles it on every `prepaint_tokens` pass,
comparing the retained span against the current token and emitting
`is_hovered: false` without needing the token (or its geometry) to still
exist. An older token's exit never clears a newer token's snapshot,
matching GPUI's enter-before-exit dispatch order. Bounds in the hover
event come from the actually placed token element, so they are correct
at soft-wrap boundaries. Exit events carry the UTF-16 coordinates
captured at entry, so JavaScript exits after a text change report the
original range instead of the new text clamped. Hover callbacks
registered through the shell keep only a weak handle to the input state,
avoiding an `Entity -> Rc callback -> Entity` cycle. All existing public
signatures keep compiling: hover uses additive builders throughout.

## Screenshot

No visual change: this is a behavior-only addition. Tokens render
exactly as before; only the new hover callback fires on pointer
entry/exit.

| Before                       | After                       |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| Tokens report clicks only | Tokens also report hover entry/exit via
`on_token_hover` |

## Public API

### `gpui-base` (`gpui_base::input`)

- `InlineTokenHoverEvent` — hover snapshot for one atomic inline token;
carries the token, its byte range, measured bounds, entry/exit state,
and entry-time UTF-16 coordinates.
- `InlineTokenHoverEvent::token(&self) -> &InlineToken` — the hovered
reference.
- `InlineTokenHoverEvent::range(&self) -> Range<usize>` — the token's
half-open UTF-8 byte range.
- `InlineTokenHoverEvent::bounds(&self) -> Bounds<Pixels>` — the token's
measured bounds, for anchoring a tooltip.
- `InlineTokenHoverEvent::is_hovered(&self) -> bool` — `true` on pointer
entry, `false` on exit.
- `InlineTokenHoverEvent::range_utf16(&self) -> (usize, usize)` — the
token range in UTF-16 code units as of entry; exits after a text change
report these.
- `InlineTokenHoverListener` — hover listener installed by a styled
control (`#[doc(hidden)]`, not part of the supported API).
- `Input::on_token_hover(listener) -> Self` — reports pointer presence
over a token in the unstyled single-line input.
- `Textarea::on_token_hover(listener) -> Self` — same, for the unstyled
multi-line textarea.
- `InputBaseState::install_token_hover_presentation(hover_listener) ->
()` — installs a styled control's token hover listener
(`#[doc(hidden)]`, not part of the supported API).

### `gpui-component` (`gpui_component::input`)

- `InlineTokenHoverEvent` — re-export of the base hover snapshot.
- `Input::on_token_hover(listener) -> Self` — reports token hover from
the styled single-line input.
- `Textarea::on_token_hover(listener) -> Self` — same, for the styled
textarea.

### `gpui-shell` (Rust adapters and JavaScript)

- `InlineTokenCallbacks::with_hover(state, hover_listener) -> Self` —
attach a hover listener to an existing callbacks adapter without
changing `new`/`apply`.
- `InlineTokenCallbacks::apply_hover(element, on_token_hover) -> E` —
install the hover listener through the element's own builder.
- `gpui_shell::inline_token_hover_data(event: &InlineTokenHoverEvent,
text: &Rope) -> Data` — converts a hover snapshot to the plain JS
payload; exits reuse the entry-time UTF-16 coordinates.
- `on_token_hover(listener)` (JavaScript, `gpui-base` NativeElement and
`gpui-component` Input/Textarea) — receives `(event:
InlineTokenHoverEvent, cx: Context)` on token entry/exit.
- `InlineTokenHoverEvent` (TypeScript, `gpui-base` and `gpui-component`
modules) — `{ token, range, hovered, bounds }` with UTF-16 ranges.

## How to Test

- `cargo test -p gpui-base inline_token` — 10 passed, including
`test_inline_token_hover_reports_presence_without_selecting` (enter/exit
payload, hover never selects, disabled suppresses entry, readonly
allows, no listener means no activation),
`test_inline_token_hover_exit_delivered_when_token_removed` (exit fires
after programmatic token removal through the real hover path),
`test_inline_token_hover_same_offset_replacement_exits_predecessor`
(replacement at the same offset exits the old token),
`test_inline_token_hover_older_exit_keeps_newer_snapshot`
(enter-B-before-exit-A ordering, then B's removal exits B), and
`test_inline_token_hover_bounds_stay_single_row_at_wrap_boundary` (hover
bounds are the laid-out element rect, not the range-extent guess).
- `cargo test -p gpui-component test_on_token_hover_builder` — 2 passed
(`Input` and `Textarea` builder coverage).
- `cargo test -p gpui-component-shell --test inline_tokens_host` —
passed, including hover entry/exit through the real mouse path with exit
coordinates (`false:3-5:a`) preserved after the click removed the token.
- `cargo test -p gpui-shell typings` — passed, including
`every_element_method_is_accounted_for`.
- `cargo check` clean for `gpui-base`, `gpui-component`, `gpui-shell`,
`gpui-component-shell`; `cargo fmt --check` and Clippy report nothing in
the touched files.

## Checklist

- [x] I have read the [CONTRIBUTING](../CONTRIBUTING.md) document and
followed the guidelines.
- [x] Reviewed the changes in this PR and confirmed AI generated code

input: report inline token hover for tooltips and previews (#3346)

Closes #3335

## Description

Adds `on_token_hover` for the atomic inline tokens rendered in `Input`
and `Textarea`, so hovering over a token can render a tooltip, preview,
or run custom logic.

The change follows the existing `on_token_click` seam: `gpui-base` owns
hover hit-testing, token geometry, and the hover snapshot event, while
`gpui-component` only forwards the builder and the application owns the
tooltip itself. Hover never selects or edits the document. Disabled
tokens never report hover entry, matching click; readonly tokens do.
Works for both `Input`/`InputState` and `Textarea`/`TextareaState`, plus
the JavaScript bindings.

Hover exit is delivered even when the hovered token is removed or
replaced programmatically (even at the same offset), scrolled out of the
laid-out rows, masked, or disabled: the state retains the last hovered
token snapshot and reconciles it on every `prepaint_tokens` pass,
comparing the retained span against the current token and emitting
`is_hovered: false` without needing the token (or its geometry) to still
exist. An older token's exit never clears a newer token's snapshot,
matching GPUI's enter-before-exit dispatch order. Bounds in the hover
event come from the actually placed token element, so they are correct
at soft-wrap boundaries. Exit events carry the UTF-16 coordinates
captured at entry, so JavaScript exits after a text change report the
original range instead of the new text clamped. Hover callbacks
registered through the shell keep only a weak handle to the input state,
avoiding an `Entity -> Rc callback -> Entity` cycle. All existing public
signatures keep compiling: hover uses additive builders throughout.

## Screenshot

No visual change: this is a behavior-only addition. Tokens render
exactly as before; only the new hover callback fires on pointer
entry/exit.

| Before                       | After                       |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| Tokens report clicks only | Tokens also report hover entry/exit via
`on_token_hover` |

## Public API

### `gpui-base` (`gpui_base::input`)

- `InlineTokenHoverEvent` — hover snapshot for one atomic inline token;
carries the token, its byte range, measured bounds, entry/exit state,
and entry-time UTF-16 coordinates.
- `InlineTokenHoverEvent::token(&self) -> &InlineToken` — the hovered
reference.
- `InlineTokenHoverEvent::range(&self) -> Range<usize>` — the token's
half-open UTF-8 byte range.
- `InlineTokenHoverEvent::bounds(&self) -> Bounds<Pixels>` — the token's
measured bounds, for anchoring a tooltip.
- `InlineTokenHoverEvent::is_hovered(&self) -> bool` — `true` on pointer
entry, `false` on exit.
- `InlineTokenHoverEvent::range_utf16(&self) -> (usize, usize)` — the
token range in UTF-16 code units as of entry; exits after a text change
report these.

control (`#[doc(hidden)]`, not part of the supported API).
- `Input::on_token_hover(listener) -> Self` — reports pointer presence
over a token in the unstyled single-line input.
- `Textarea::on_token_hover(listener) -> Self` — same, for the unstyled
multi-line textarea.

()` — installs a styled control's token hover listener
(`#[doc(hidden)]`, not part of the supported API).

### `gpui-component` (`gpui_component::input`)

- `InlineTokenHoverEvent` — re-export of the base hover snapshot.
- `Input::on_token_hover(listener) -> Self` — reports token hover from

changing `new`/`apply`.

install the hover listener through the element's own builder.

commit.message:
input: Keep horizontal scrolling and soft wrapping consistent (#3358)

Closes #3357

## Description

Deleting text near the viewport width in Input could paint with a
horizontal offset different from the retained scroll state. Textarea
could also shift or clip text near a soft-wrap boundary, and continued
Latin input after Chinese text could move an already-fitting Chinese
character onto the next row.

Clamp horizontal scrolling before positioning text and every caret,
using the same range as retained state. Resolve ordinary text wrapping
from Unicode line-break opportunities and shaped prefix widths in the
shared display map, with grapheme-safe fallback for oversized words.
Preserve the existing inline-element wrapping path. The
`unicode-linebreak` dependency uses the version already present in the
workspace lockfile. No public API changes.

## Screenshot

Before: the two reproductions attached to #3357.

After — Textarea: Chinese IME composition, commit, and soft wrapping
(2026-10-03 16:23:55):


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/85cc8f37-f4bf-4d3a-ab33-2bb4c4e89005

After — Input: deletion while horizontally scrolled (2026-10-03
16:24:34):


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/77c9b8e5-4ecd-4b49-9a79-130704621359

## How to Test

Validation completed locally on macOS 27.0.1:

- `cargo build -p gpui-component-story --locked` passed; launched the
Input and Textarea stories.
- `cargo test -p gpui-base --lib
horizontal_scroll_is_clamped_before_text_and_caret_layout --locked`
passed (1 test).
- `cargo test -p gpui-base --lib
input::display_map::text_wrapper::tests` passed (15 tests), including
incremental `abcd的 → abcd的s → abcd的ss → backspace` coverage, cursor row
mapping, word boundaries, punctuation, emoji, indentation, and narrow
widths.
- `rustfmt --check --edition 2024 --config skip_children=true` on the
three changed Rust files and `git diff --check` passed.
- The reporter manually verified single-line deletion and Textarea
Chinese IME composition/wrapping, and confirmed both fixes.
Windows/Linux native behavior and performance have not been tested
locally.

To reproduce: enter text beyond the width of the default Input and
repeatedly delete it; then type Chinese text up to a Textarea line end,
append Latin letters, and exercise IME composition, commit, and
backspace across the wrapping boundary.

## Checklist

- [x] I have read the CONTRIBUTING document and followed the guidelines.
- [x] Reviewed the changes; implementation and regression tests were
AI-assisted, and the reporter verified the resulting UI behavior.
- [x] Built and launched the related stories; manually verified Input
and Textarea on macOS.
- [ ] Tested Windows and Linux platform behavior/performance.

commit.message:
editor: Measure the completion prefix from the typed text and drop stale trigger offsets (#3363)

Closes #3081

## Description

`InputBaseState::<EditorMode>::handle_completion_trigger` hands the
completion provider the wrong `trigger_character` in two ways, both
reported in #3081 with repro steps against `examples/editor`.

**The replacement was measured from `range.end`.** That only locates the
typed text for a collapsed caret. When a keystroke replaces a span
(typing over a selection, an IME commit) the new text begins at
`range.start`, so an equally long replacement measured an empty prefix
and a longer one made `new_offset < start_offset` true and dropped the
request before the provider was called. The handler now derives the
inserted text's start from the post-edit active caret and the normalized
input length. This also accounts for preceding multi-cursor edits
shifting the active insertion, while preserving selection replacements
and IME commits.

**`trigger_start_offset` was a latch that nothing invalidated.** Once a
menu opened it was reused by every later keystroke: not a deletion, not
`hide_context_menu()`, not a document switch cleared it. Typing a
character at offset 0 latched `Some(0)`, and from then on every
keystroke anywhere measured `text[0..caret]`. The latch now applies only
while the edit continues the word it was opened for: the document
between the latched offset and the edit must still read as a prefix of
the last recorded query. Deleting back into the word keeps refining the
same query (`pri` → backspace → `v` still asks for `prv`); typing
somewhere else, or into a replaced document, starts a new query at the
edit.

The check lives in the handler rather than in `hide_context_menu()`
because `replace_text_in_ranges` hides the menu on every edit, including
the keystroke that is about to refine the query; clearing the latch
there would reduce every query to its last character.
`present_completion_items` and the component menu's own
`trigger_start_offset` are unchanged.

## How to Test

```sh
cargo test -p gpui-kit --features "test-support component" --test input completions::
```

New cases in `crates/kit/tests/input/completions.rs`:

-
`typing_over_a_selection_measures_the_prefix_from_where_the_text_begins`:
without the fix the longer replacement sends no request and the
equal-length one sends `trigger_character: ""`.
- `typing_elsewhere_does_not_reuse_a_stale_trigger_offset`: without the
fix the provider receives `"!\na"` instead of `"a"`.
- `replacing_the_document_starts_a_new_query_at_the_edit`: without the
fix the provider receives `"hellox"` instead of `"x"`.
- `deleting_back_into_the_word_keeps_refining_the_same_query`: guards
the refinement path the latch exists for; passes before and after.

All 45 `completions::` tests pass.

A follow-up regression,
`test_multicursor_unicode_completion_uses_post_edit_start` in Base,
reproduces a UTF-8 boundary panic when another cursor inserts Chinese
text before the active cursor. It failed before the follow-up fix and
passes afterward, checking both the provider's post-edit offset and
query. The handler also validates both slice endpoints. Local follow-up
validation passed: all 1,307 Base library tests, all 45 Kit
`completions::` tests, targeted Base/Kit Clippy with warnings denied,
and formatting/diff checks. Follow-up implementation and regression test
were AI-assisted with Codex. CI for the follow-up commit is pending.
Also run: `cargo clippy -p gpui-base -p gpui-kit --features
"gpui-kit/test-support gpui-kit/component" --all-targets -- --deny
warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, and `cargo test -p gpui-component --lib
input::` for the overlay that mirrors the trigger offset.

Not a visual change, so no screenshots. The headless UI tests above
cover the behavior; I did not run the story app for this.

AI assistance: the analysis, patch and tests were drafted with Claude
(Fable 5.1) in Claude Code and reviewed by me before submission.

## Checklist

- [x] I have read the [CONTRIBUTING](../CONTRIBUTING.md) document and
followed the guidelines.
- [x] Reviewed the changes in this PR and confirmed AI generated code
(If any) is accurate.
- [ ] Passed `cargo run` for story tests related to the changes. (Not
run: no story exercises completion triggers; covered by the headless
`completions::` tests.)
- [x] Tested macOS, Windows and Linux platforms performance (if the
change is platform-specific). Not platform-specific, but verified
anyway: the PR's CI run
[37157842358](https://github.com/longbridge/gpui-kit/actions/runs/37157842358)
passed `Test (aarch64-apple-darwin, macos-latest)`, `Test
(x86_64-linux-gnu, ubuntu-latest)` and `Test (x86_64-windows-msvc,
windows-latest)` along with Lint, No default features and the GPUI Shell
jobs; locally the 45 `completions::` tests pass on macOS 15 (Apple
Silicon) and inside a Linux container (`rust:1-bookworm`, aarch64, rustc
1.99.0, deps from `script/install-linux.sh`).




### Follow-up: asynchronous completion menu refresh

A reported `c` → `co` workflow exposed a state-feedback race:
synchronizing a hidden Component popup scheduled a dismissal back to
Base, which could close a newer completion response. Presentation-only
hiding now leaves Base untouched; explicit user dismissal still notifies
Base. A deterministic regression failed before this fix and passes
afterward. Also verified 46 Kit completion workflows, 40 Component input
tests, targeted Component/Kit Clippy, formatting/diff checks, and an
editor example rebuild. Follow-up code and tests were AI-assisted with
Codex. CI for this revision is pending.
